newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Calm returns to crowded Sarajevo polling booths.
newsitem.headline: Calm returns to crowded Sarajevo polling booths.

text.p: A number of polling stations in Sarajevo which were closed temporarily on Saturday because of crowd problems were reopened after NATO troops restored order, an alliance spokesman said.
Eight balloting centres in the densely populated Novi Grad highrise district closed just before midday to sort out organisational glitches, but they reopened two hours later.

NATO Major Brett Boudreau told a news briefing that earlier reports of impatient voters smashing windows and kicking in doors appeared to have been incorrect. He said windows shattered from the pressure of crowds leaning on them.
"The situation is calm now," he said.

He said a French unit of the NATO-led peace Implementation Force (IFOR) and U.N. police went to the district at the request of election supervisors to reinstate order after crowds of waiting voters threatened to swell out of control.
Organisers said voting in the district might be extended beyond the official 7 p.m. (1700 gmt) close to make up for the midday closure.
Some delays in Bosnia's first postwar elections may have been caused by strict measures, involving the spraying of invisible ink, to prevent multiple voting.
Some voters have also needed time for explanations of secret-ballot procedure and a plethora of choices on separate ballot forms corresponding to four tiers of government.
